relevance_note: Case report of a woman with a LAMP2 variant and Danon disease: "whole-exome sequencing (WES) identified the novel A to T transition in initiation codon (c.1A > T) of LAMP2 gene, establishing the diagnosis of DD".
method_note: Written by hand, assembled with a short Python script (no table transcription by script). Labels: pedigree labels from Supplementary Figure 1 legend (IIIA proband, IVA son, IIB mother). Previously published patient of reference (7) (Antukh D, et al., 2020; 23-year-old man with Danon disease and PYP false positivity) included under the v4 passing-mention rule (sex, age, features given); no LAMP2 variant is printed or tied to him, so no variant row. Not given rows: the c.2T > C patient(s) of Wang et al. (15) (only a variant mentioned, no person described); the proband's three miscarriages (no individuals described); the 472 ClinVar variants mentioned in the Discussion. Proband variant type recorded as 'other' from 'initiation codon mutation'; the paper also notes ClinVar calls it a 'missense initiation codon variant' and predicts a frameshift via downstream ATG, so the class is ambiguous. ACMG criteria recorded verbatim as printed 'PSV1 + PM2'. MutationTaster and AlphaFold predictions are in silico, not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Son (IVA): carrier of 'this LAMP2 mutation' by NGS; c.1A > T taken as the variant string because the sentence refers to the proband's variant; inheritance 'inherited maternal' because his mother (the proband) is stated to carry the variant; zygosity, type, pathogenicity and ACMG left 'not reported' (stated for the proband's variant, not for him). Mother (IIB): not tested; 'likely attributable to this same LAMP2 variant' is not a carrier statement, so no variant row; her hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is hedged ('suspected'), recorded as an observed feature with 'suspected' in the text but the LVH checklist item left 'not reported'. Contradictions/inconsistencies: abstract says acute heart failure post cesarean section 'at age 29' while Table 1 gives '2019/08/23, aged 28' (feature onset left null); mother died 'at age 30' (case presentation) vs 'around age 30' (Discussion). The text uses 'ECG' for echocardiography and 'EKG' for electrocardiogram. 'No clinical sign of heart failure' on admission recorded as an excluded feature for that time point; the heart failure checklist item stays 'observed' from the earlier episode (temporal, not a contradiction). Checklist 'intellectual disability, cognitive impairment or learning difficulties' left 'not reported' for the proband: 'no cognitive deficits' is recorded as an excluded feature, but the composite item's other parts are not addressed and the paper says intelligence assessment was not done. 'Without extracardiac symptoms' recorded as stated, excluding nothing more specific. Laboratory table (Supplementary Table 1) values not flagged by the authors as abnormal (e.g. NT-proBNP) were not recorded as features. Proband vital status 'alive' from the 2-year follow-up echocardiography. Age at last evaluation '30-year-old' is the age at presentation; age at the 2-year follow-up is not stated. n_patients_reported left null (no number stated).
